column1: # What the strip should put first for an English word, one case per line: typed<TAB>expected.
# Read by native-tests/suggest_eval. Not a test and nothing here asserts: the number it prints is
# a measurement that moves when a scoring constant moves, which is the only way to price a change
# that helps one case and hurts another.
# Where the right answer is to leave the word alone, the expectation is the typed word itself.
# "offers nothing better than what I wrote" is a result worth measuring, and it is the one the
# guards in AutoCorrection exist to produce.
# The case this file was created for. "the" is the commonest word in English and one
# transposition away, and it currently ranks below "tehachapi" and "tehsildar".
# --- words that must be left exactly as written ---------------------------------------------
# Each of these is a real word, and a keyboard that rewrites real words is the failure this
# project was written against. They are the cost side of any change to the edit penalty: a
# value low enough to fix the block above must not break this one.
# --- a finished word must not lose to a longer one that starts with it ----------------------
# Measured at the current constants: typing "car" offers "care", "cartea", "carol" and "carmen",
# and "car" itself is nowhere in the sixteen kept -- though it is in both dictionaries. A
# completion costs 0.12 per added character, which is not enough to beat being commoner, so the
# word actually typed loses to words merely beginning with it. kCompletionPenalty governs this.
# --- half-typed words, where completing IS the right answer ---------------------------------
# The cost side of kCompletionPenalty. Without these the corpus only rewards raising it, and a
# value that makes a finished word win would quietly stop the keyboard finishing an unfinished
# one -- which is most of what the strip is for while a word is still being typed.
# --- regressions named in the constants' own comments ---------------------------------------
# kTransposeCost's comment: too cheap a transposition let "acm" reach "cam" and crowd every
# insertion-based candidate out of the sixteen kept, including "acum" itself.
# The completion-past-a-correction comment: a frequent inflected relative of a corrected word
# outscored the correction. Romanian, so it only measures with the ro-RO pack loaded.
# "snobul" is deliberately absent from this file. It is AutoCorrection's case, not the engine's:
# the word is in neither pack, so the engine cannot offer it and no ranking change can help. What
# leaves it alone is the guard in correctionFor, which AutoCorrectionTest already covers.
